run.notes: Concurrency sweep on gemma4:e2b-it-qat-text, the projector-free variant. THIS IS THE LIKE-FOR-LIKE RUN against local-llamacpp-1650ti-2b-q4_0's 2026-09-03-full-sweep-1650ti: both servers are llama-server at -c 32768 with 32 slots of 1024 tokens, all KV in VRAM, 36/36 layers offloaded. The earlier 2026-09-04-first-light-ollama-1650ti run could not reach that geometry because the stock tag's projector forced 2048 tokens/slot and the result did not fit the card.

hardware.accelerator: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti with Max-Q Design

host.notes: TU117, compute capability 7.5, NO tensor cores. Max-Q: thermally throttled.

model.architecture_notes: `ollama show --modelfile gemma4:e2b-it-qat` with the second FROM removed and nothing else changed: same model blob by digest, same RENDERER/PARSER gemma4, same three sampling parameters, projector layer dropped. Capabilities go from 'completion vision audio tools thinking' to 'completion tools thinking'. Reasoning model: every cell measures the thinking phase at 128 output tokens.

software.notes: Child process: llama-server -c 32768 -np 32 --flash-attn auto -b 512 -ub 512 --context-shift --keep 4 --no-jinja --chat-template chatml. The sibling ran llama-server -c 32768 --parallel 32 with llama.cpp's DEFAULT batch sizes (-b 2048 -ub 512), which is the one server-flag difference remaining between the two runs and the leading candidate for the TTFT/TPOT trade at c=16 and c=32.

memory.notes: 2106 MiB of 4096 at 32 slots, 36/36 layers on GPU, all KV in VRAM (192 MiB non-SWA + 384 MiB SWA). At 1 slot / 8192 context the same model is 1612 MiB, against 2762 for the stock tag and 1618 for the llama.cpp sibling. `ollama ps` never counts the projector, so it under-reports by ~1150 MiB on the stock tag and by 181-291 MiB (CUDA context + compute buffers, scaling with slots) here.

workload.tool: sweep.py (copy of the llama.cpp sibling's, three bugs fixed)
workload.notes: decode-source auto -> stream. Prompt cache defeated by --prompt-mode shuffled; the sibling used cache_prompt:false, which Ollama drops in translation. Both verified to cached=0.

issues.summary: Ollama applies a MINIMUM PER-SLOT CONTEXT OF 2048 to projector-carrying models and none to text-only ones. MEASURED across four settings: the stock tag took 1024->2048 and 1536->2048 (and honoured 8192), while the text-only variant honoured 1024, 1536 and 8192 exactly. This is what made the stock tag unable to hold 32 slots on a 4 GiB card.

TTFT grows sub-linearly on this runtime past c=8 (ratios 1.73 and 1.64 per doubling against the sibling's 2.01 and 1.90) while TPOT roughly doubles relative to it (144.82/376.90 against 96.97/184.36). Aggregate throughput is unchanged, so it is a scheduling redistribution rather than a throughput difference. NOT isolated -- Ollama forces -b 512 where llama.cpp defaults to 2048.

notes: LIKE-FOR-LIKE against 2026-09-03-full-sweep-1650ti at identical server geometry. c=1 through c=8 agree within 4%: 32.55/32.74, 39.72/40.59, 43.35/45.12, 46.18/44.79 tok/s aggregate. Peak is 46.18 here against 48.19 there, both saturating near 45-48.

TTFT doubles with c through c=8 on BOTH runtimes -- 2114/4164/8393/15978 here, 2135/4062/7982/16212 there -- so prefill runs one request at a time and concurrency past c=4-8 buys latency and nothing else. That is the load-bearing result and it is the same on both.
The c=8 cells are the noisy ones on both sides: 6.9% spread here, 7.7% there. This part is Max-Q and throttles; never read a single row.
Not comparable to the T4-based g4dn/g5g rigs at equal compute capability 7.5: TU117 has no tensor cores, TU104 does.
